title: Roof Replacement / Re-Roofing
metaDescription: Apex Roofing full roof replacement and re-roofing: process, materials, timelines and warranties.
intro: A complete re-roof is the biggest roofing decision most homeowners make. We make it straightforward: documented inspection, an itemised written quote, and most homes finished in 2 to 4 days.

sections.heading: What a re-roof includes
bullets: Full strip of the existing roof covering
Inspection of timbers and repairs quoted transparently
Breathable underlay, battens and new fixings
Your choice of concrete tile, clay tile or natural slate
Ridge, hip and valley components measured and itemised where required
Removal and disposal of all old materials, site left clean

sections.heading: How the price is built
body: Roof size, pitch, material and access drive the price. Strip and disposal are allowance-based and confirmed after inspection. Our Smart Assistant can give you an indicative ballpark in about a minute - just ask.

sections.heading: Timelines
body: Most single-storey and two-storey homes are stripped and re-covered in 2 to 4 working days, weather permitting. Scaffolding goes up the day before and comes down within a week of completion.

title: New Roof Installation
metaDescription: New roof installation for new builds, extensions and conversions by Apex Roofing.
intro: Building new? We install complete roof systems for new builds, extensions, garages and conversions, working alongside your builder to your drawings and specification.

sections.heading: What we cover
bullets: New build roofs to architect specification
Extension and conversion roofs
Tile, slate and flat membrane systems
Fascia, soffit, guttering and downpipes
Insulation integrated at installation time

sections.heading: Working with your build schedule
body: We coordinate with your main contractor so the roof is watertight at the right stage of the build. Fixed-price quotes from drawings, with any variations agreed in writing before work proceeds.

title: Roof Repairs
metaDescription: Roof repair services: leaks, slipped tiles and slates, flashing and valley repairs by Apex Roofing.
intro: Most roof problems are smaller than they look from the ground. We find the real cause, fix it properly, and back repairs with a 2-year workmanship warranty.

sections.heading: Common repairs
bullets: Leak tracing and permanent fixes
Slipped, cracked or broken tiles and slates
Ridge and hip repointing or dry-fix upgrade
Flashing and chimney repairs
Valley trough repair and replacement
Storm damage make-safe and follow-on repairs

sections.heading: Pricing
body: A standard repair visit is a fixed fee covering investigation and replacement of up to 10 tiles or slates or a minor flashing repair. Larger work is quoted after inspection. Ask the Smart Assistant for the current repair rate.

title: Flat Roofing
metaDescription: Flat and low-slope roofing systems: GRP fibreglass, EPDM and membrane by Apex Roofing.
intro: Flat roofs fail when they are poorly detailed, not when they are flat. We install modern systems with correct falls and detailing so garages, extensions and dormers stay dry for decades.

sections.heading: Systems we install
bullets: GRP fibreglass - seamless and extremely durable
EPDM rubber membrane - flexible and long-lived
High-performance felt systems for budget-sensitive projects
Insulated warm-deck upgrades

sections.heading: Pitch matters
body: Flat roofs are never truly flat. Building a minimum fall avoids ponding, which is the main cause of premature failure. We check and correct falls during installation.

title: Guttering & Downpipes
metaDescription: Guttering, downpipes, fascia and soffit replacement by Apex Roofing, including drainage upgrades alongside re-roofing work.
intro: Gutters protect more than the roof. We replace guttering, downpipes, fascias and soffits either as a standalone job or as part of your re-roof, when access is already in place.

sections.heading: What we install
bullets: Half-round PVC gutter systems in common colours
Downpipes with offsets, shoes and brackets
UPVC fascia and vented soffit boards
Replacement outlets, unions and brackets
Leaf protection where it suits the property

sections.heading: Standalone work or part of a re-roof
body: Gutters, downpipes, fascia and soffit can be handled as a standalone job or added while a roof is already being replaced. Combining the work can reduce duplicated access and labour.

sections.heading: Sizing and drainage
body: The right gutter and downpipe arrangement depends on roof area, rainfall, outlet positions and the existing drainage route. If a drainage question needs site-specific calculations, the Apex team will confirm it rather than the Smart Assistant guessing.

title: Roofing Materials
metaDescription: Guide to Apex Roofing materials: concrete and clay tile, natural slate, shingles, metal roofing, flat-roof systems and supporting roof components.
intro: The material you choose affects cost, appearance, pitch suitability and lifespan. Apex works with pitched-roof coverings, flat-roof systems and the supporting components that make the complete roof work.

sections.heading: Concrete and clay tiles
body: Concrete tiles are durable, widely available and generally the best-value traditional pitched-roof option. Clay tiles cost more but offer a distinctive finish and long service life.

sections.heading: Natural slate
body: Natural slate is a premium pitched-roof covering with a long service life. Apex uses natural Spanish slate in the configured demo systems and fixes slate with suitable corrosion-resistant fixings.

sections.heading: Shingles and metal roofing
body: For suitable pitched roofs, Apex can discuss asphalt shingles, pressed metal tiles and long-run profiled metal. Pitch, exposure, detailing and the chosen manufacturer system need to be checked before a formal specification is confirmed.

sections.heading: Flat-roof systems
body: Apex installs EPDM rubber and GRP fibreglass systems for suitable flat and low-slope roofs. High-performance felt can also be assessed, but some felt projects need a site-specific specification rather than an instant online price.

sections.heading: What sits underneath and around the covering
body: A complete roof also relies on underlay or membrane, battens or deck support, suitable fixings, ridge and hip systems, valleys, flashings, gutters, downpipes, fascia and soffit. Those items can be discussed separately or as part of a roof project.

sections.heading: Not sure what suits your roof?
body: Ask the Smart Assistant to compare options for your roof type and pitch. If the answer depends on site conditions or a manufacturer-specific detail, it will hand the question to the Apex team rather than guess.

title: Concrete vs Clay vs Slate
metaDescription: Side-by-side comparison of concrete tile, clay tile and natural slate roofing.
intro: Three great coverings, three different trade-offs. Here is the honest comparison.

sections.heading: Cost
body: Concrete is the most economical per square metre, clay sits in the middle, and natural slate is the premium option. All three are installed to the same standard by Apex.

sections.heading: Appearance
body: Concrete tiles suit most modern homes. Clay has warmth and character that improves with age. Slate delivers a sharp, premium look favoured on period and high-end properties.

sections.heading: Lifespan and durability
bullets: Concrete tile: around 40+ years, very low maintenance
Clay tile: around 50+ years, colour-stable
Natural slate: 75 to 100+ years, exceptional when properly fixed

sections.heading: Pitch suitability
body: All three need adequate roof pitch. Slate in particular generally requires a steeper roof than interlocking concrete tiles. Very low-pitch roofs are better served by membrane systems. See our roof pitch guide.

title: Roof Pitch Guide
metaDescription: What roof pitch means, typical pitch bands, and why pitch affects material choice and price.
intro: Pitch is the angle of your roof slope, measured in degrees from horizontal. It changes which materials you can use and how the roof is priced.

sections.heading: Typical bands
bullets: Flat / Low: 0 to 15 degrees
Medium: 16 to 35 degrees - most family homes
Steep: 36 degrees and above - period properties, complex roofs

sections.heading: Why pitch matters
bullets: Material minimum pitches: slate needs a steeper roof than interlocking concrete tiles
Steeper roofs have more actual roof area per square metre of floor, so covering costs more
Steep roofs are slower and safer-access work can affect labour
Very low slopes need membrane systems rather than tiles

sections.heading: Plan area vs roof area
body: A 100 m² footprint at a steeper pitch has more actual sloped roof area than the same footprint at a low pitch. Our estimator accounts for this when you tell us the pitch.

title: How Roofing Estimates Work
metaDescription: How Apex Roofing builds estimates: roof area, material, pitch, components and allowances.
intro: A credible estimate is built from measurable inputs, not guesswork. Here is exactly what goes into ours.

sections.heading: The inputs
bullets: Roof area, and whether it is the actual sloped area or the footprint
Pitch, exact or by band

sections.heading: New roof vs re-roof

sections.heading: Indicative vs formal
body: Our Smart Assistant gives indicative ballparks instantly from approved rates. A formal quotation follows a free site inspection and confirmed measurements. Want a quick figure? Ask the assistant for a guided estimate.

title: Re-Roof Cost Guide
metaDescription: What a re-roof costs and what is involved: strip and disposal allowances, covering systems, components, timelines and how to get an itemised ballpark from the Apex Smart Assistant.
intro: A straight answer on re-roof costs. Covering system rates depend on material and roof size; on top of those, every re-roof adds strip and disposal allowances. Here is how the price is built.

sections.heading: Covering system rates (supply and installed)
bullets: Concrete tile - from £62 per m²
Clay tile - from £78 per m²

sections.heading: Re-roof allowances every quote includes
bullets: Strip existing roof - £10 per m² (indicative, confirmed after inspection)

sections.heading: What drives the final price
bullets: Roof size (measured on the actual sloped surface, not the footprint)

title: Roofing FAQ
metaDescription: Frequently asked roofing questions answered by Apex Roofing.
intro: The questions we hear most, answered plainly.

sections.heading: How long does a re-roof take?
body: Most homes are completed in 2 to 4 working days, weather permitting.

sections.heading: Will you need scaffolding?
body: Usually yes for full replacements. Standard single-storey access is included in our rates. Anything beyond that is quoted transparently.

sections.heading: What if it rains during the work?
body: We strip and re-cover in sections and use temporary protection so your home stays watertight overnight.

sections.heading: How messy is it?
body: Messy for a day or two, but all waste is removed and the site swept before handover.

sections.heading: Do you offer finance?
body: Not directly. In a live deployment this answer would come from the business's approved data - ask the Smart Assistant for current options.

sections.heading: Do you work in winter?
body: Yes, with common-sense limits. Frost and heavy rain can delay tiling for safety and quality reasons.

sections.heading: How accurate are online estimates?
body: Indicative estimates use approved rates and your inputs. Final prices follow a free inspection, because timber condition and access cannot be seen from a photo.

title: Pitched Roof Coverings
metaDescription: Concrete tile, clay tile, natural slate, asphalt shingles, pressed metal tile and long-run metal roofing options from Apex Roofing.
intro: Different pitched-roof coverings suit different roof angles, budgets and architectural styles. This guide shows the main options Apex can discuss and where a site-specific check is still needed.

sections.heading: Concrete tile
body: A durable, cost-effective choice for many UK pitched roofs. The configured Apex demo system includes breathable underlay, battens, fixings, dry verge and installation.

sections.heading: Clay tile
body: A traditional covering with strong character and long service life. The exact profile and minimum pitch must suit the roof and the selected manufacturer system.

sections.heading: Natural slate
body: A premium covering with a long service life. Correct headlap, batten gauge, fixing pattern and skilled installation are important.

sections.heading: Asphalt shingles
body: A lightweight pitched-roof option used on suitable roofs and structures. Deck condition, underlayment and pitch need to be checked before specification.

sections.heading: Pressed metal tile
body: Pressed metal tiles provide a tiled appearance with a lighter roof covering. Support spacing, fixings and exposure requirements depend on the selected system.

sections.heading: Long-run profiled metal
body: Long-run metal can suit lower-pitch and contemporary roofs when the chosen profile, laps, fixings and exposure rating are appropriate. Final specification is manufacturer and site dependent.

title: Flat Roof Systems
metaDescription: EPDM, GRP fibreglass and high-performance felt flat-roof options, detailing and survey considerations from Apex Roofing.
intro: Flat roofs rely on continuous waterproof systems, correct falls and careful detailing at edges, outlets and upstands. Apex can install or repair several common systems.

sections.heading: EPDM rubber membrane
body: EPDM is a flexible sheet membrane commonly used on extensions, garages and other suitable flat roofs. Deck condition, falls, edges and outlets are checked as part of the job.

sections.heading: GRP fibreglass
body: GRP forms a rigid, seamless fibreglass surface when installed onto a suitable deck. It is often chosen where a crisp finished appearance and robust surface are wanted.

sections.heading: High-performance felt
body: Modern felt systems can be appropriate on some flat roofs. Because build-up, deck, insulation, outlets and detailing vary, Apex may need a survey before confirming the exact system or price.

sections.heading: What cannot be confirmed remotely
body: Hidden deck condition, insulation build-up, structural falls, outlet capacity and awkward perimeter details can change the specification. The Smart Assistant can explain the options, but the team confirms site-specific details.

title: Underlay, Battens & Roof Decking
metaDescription: Apex Roofing guide to breathable underlay, battens, support layers and flat-roof decking.
intro: The visible roof covering is only one part of the system. Underlay, battens and deck support help manage water, ventilation and the loads transferred into the roof structure.

sections.heading: Breathable underlay and membranes
body: Apex uses breathable membrane in the configured full pitched-roof systems. It forms a secondary water-shedding layer beneath tiles or slate while allowing the roof build-up to manage moisture correctly.

sections.heading: Battens
body: Timber battens support tile and slate coverings. Their spacing depends on the chosen product, headlap and roof pitch, so final gauge is set to the actual roof and manufacturer instructions.

sections.heading: Metal-roof support layers
body: Pressed and long-run metal systems can require specific support spacing, membranes and fixing arrangements. The exact build-up is confirmed for the selected profile and exposure.

sections.heading: Flat-roof decking
body: EPDM, GRP and felt systems rely on a sound, suitable deck. Existing deck condition cannot be guaranteed from a photo or chat conversation and may need inspection before a formal quote.

title: Roof Fixings & Components
metaDescription: Dry-fix ridge and hip systems, valleys, flashings, roof fixings and associated components used by Apex Roofing.
intro: A roof covering only performs properly when its fixings, edges, junctions and drainage details are right. Apex treats these components as part of the roofing system, not afterthoughts.

sections.heading: Tile, slate and metal fixings
body: Fixings vary by covering. The configured demo systems include suitable tile fixings, copper slate nails and metal-system fixings where relevant. Final fixing patterns depend on product and exposure requirements.

sections.heading: Dry-fix ridge, hip and verge
body: Mechanically fixed ridge, hip and verge systems avoid reliance on exposed mortar and can provide controlled ventilation where the system is designed for it.

sections.heading: Valleys and flashings
body: Apex works with GRP valley troughs and lead or aluminium flashings at roof junctions, chimneys, walls and abutments. These details are common leak points when damaged or badly installed.

sections.heading: Fascia, soffit, gutters and downpipes
body: Roof-edge components and drainage can be replaced separately or alongside a re-roof. Exact drainage sizing and unusual details are confirmed by the team when a site-specific answer is needed.
